states.claim: conn is a non-NULL PGconn pointer; NULL is rejected at entry.
states.evidence:
L9: if (conn == NULL)
L10: return PGRES_POLLING_FAILED;

states.claim: conn->addrlist is released by release_conn_addrinfo(conn) before being replaced for a new host.
conn->addrlist is set by pg_getaddrinfo_all() for the selected host type and is non-NULL on success.
conn->addr_cur points into the conn->addrlist addrinfo chain; it is advanced to ai_next or reset to conn->addrlist.
states.evidence:
L69: conn->addr_cur = conn->addr_cur->ai_next;
L203: conn->addr_cur = conn->addrlist;

states.claim: conn->connip is freed and set to NULL before being optionally replaced by strdup(host_addr).
conn->sock is assigned the result of socket(); PGINVALID_SOCKET indicates failure.
states.evidence:
L299: conn->sock = socket(addr_cur->ai_family, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
L300: if (conn->sock == PGINVALID_SOCKET)

states.claim: pqDropConnection(conn, true) drops any existing connection and pqDropServerData(conn) resets server-derived state before a new connection attempt.
conn->asyncStatus is reset to PGASYNC_IDLE when forcing a new connection.
conn->status is set to CONNECTION_NEEDED when forcing a new connection.
conn->raddr.addr and conn->raddr.salen are filled from the current addrinfo entry.
conn->laddr.addr and conn->laddr.salen are filled by getsockname() on conn->sock.
states.evidence:
L540: conn->laddr.salen = sizeof(conn->laddr.addr);
L541: if (getsockname(conn->sock,
L542: (struct sockaddr *) &conn->laddr.addr,
L543: &conn->laddr.salen) < 0)

states.claim: startpacket is allocated by pqBuildStartupPacket3() and freed after use or on send failure.
conn->gcred may be set by pg_GSS_have_cred_cache() when GSS credentials are available.
conn->inStart is advanced to conn->inCursor to mark consumed input bytes.
res is a PGresult pointer returned by PQgetResult(); non-NULL results are cleared with PQclear().
conn->addrlist is released by release_conn_addrinfo(conn) after target checks succeed.
conn->errorMessage is reset by resetPQExpBuffer() on successful connection.
conn->status is set to CONNECTION_BAD on error_return.

values.claim: sebuf is a char array of size PG_STRERROR_R_BUFLEN, used as the error-string buffer passed with sizeof(sebuf) to SOCK_STRERROR/strerror_r.
portstr is a char array of size MAXPGPATH; thisport is formatted into it with snprintf bounded by sizeof(portstr).
values.evidence:
L84: char		portstr[MAXPGPATH];
L140: snprintf(portstr, sizeof(portstr), "%d", thisport);

values.claim: thisport is constrained to the range 1..65535 when parsed from ch->port; otherwise it defaults to DEF_PGPORT.
values.evidence:
L126: thisport = DEF_PGPORT;
L132: if (thisport < 1 || thisport > 65535)

values.claim: After UNIXSOCK_PATH(portstr, thisport, ch->host), strlen(portstr) is checked to be < UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN; the error message reports the maximum as UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN - 1.
conn->whichhost is advanced only when conn->whichhost + 1 < conn->nconnhost; otherwise it is reset to 0 in prefer-standby pass2 or an error is taken.
ch points to conn->connhost[conn->whichhost], so the index is bounded by the whichhost/nconnhost relation.
conn->raddr.addr is filled by memcpy of addr_cur->ai_addrlen bytes from addr_cur->ai_addr, and conn->raddr.salen is set to that same length.
host_addr is a char array of size NI_MAXHOST passed to getHostaddr with that size.
values.evidence:
L268: char		host_addr[NI_MAXHOST];
L294: getHostaddr(conn, host_addr, NI_MAXHOST);

conn->laddr.salen is initialized to sizeof(conn->laddr.addr) before getsockname writes the client address into conn->laddr.addr.

values.claim: startpacket is allocated by pqBuildStartupPacket3, which sets packetlen; pqPacketSend is then called with startpacket and packetlen.
msgLength is reduced by 4, then avail = conn->inEnd - conn->inCursor; if avail < msgLength, pqCheckInBufferSpace is called with conn->inCursor + (size_t) msgLength.
For beresp == 'R', msgLength must be in [8, 2000]; for beresp == 'E', msgLength must be in [8, 30000] or the pre-3.0 error path is taken.
values.evidence:
L1058: if (beresp == 'R' && (msgLength < 8 || msgLength > 2000))
L1066: if (beresp == 'E' && (msgLength < 8 || msgLength > 30000))

values.claim: After reading areq with pqGetInt(...,4,...), msgLength is reduced by 4 and passed to pg_fe_sendauth.
The last byte of conn->errorMessage.data is accessed at index conn->errorMessage.len - 1 only when len > 0 (or len != 0).

values.claim: conn->sversion < 90000 causes conn->in_hot_standby to be set to PG_BOOL_NO.

executions.claim: Continuing past the initial NULL check implies conn is non-NULL.
executions.evidence:
L9: if (conn == NULL)
L10: return PGRES_POLLING_FAILED;

executions.claim: Continuing past the first switch implies conn->status is not CONNECTION_BAD or CONNECTION_OK.
When conn->try_next_addr is true and conn->addr_cur has no next address, conn->try_next_host is set true.
executions.evidence:
L65: if (conn->try_next_addr)
L67: if (conn->addr_cur && conn->addr_cur->ai_next)

L73: conn->try_next_host = true;

executions.claim: When conn->try_next_host is true and there are no more hosts, execution either resets to prefer-standby pass 2 with whichhost=0 or goes to error_return.
If ch->port is NULL or empty, thisport is DEF_PGPORT; otherwise parse_int_param must succeed and thisport must be in [1,65535] to continue.
After address resolution, conn->addrlist is non-NULL and ret is zero for the selected host type.
After successful host setup, conn->addr_cur is set to conn->addrlist.
executions.evidence: L203: conn->addr_cur = conn->addrlist;

executions.claim: If socket creation fails and there are more addresses or hosts, execution continues; otherwise it goes to error_return.
For non-Unix sockets, connectNoDelay, pg_set_noblock, and fcntl(F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) must succeed to continue.

executions.claim: If connect returns EINPROGRESS, EWOULDBLOCK (WIN32), or EINTR, status becomes CONNECTION_STARTED and returns PGRES_POLLING_WRITING; otherwise connect failure leads to try_next_addr.
In CONNECTION_STARTED, getsockopt(SO_ERROR) must succeed and optval must be zero to continue.

L520: goto error_return;
L522: else if (optval != 0)

executions.evidence:

executions.claim: If requirepeer is set and the address is Unix-domain, getpeereid must succeed and the peer user name must match requirepeer.
If GSS is enabled and try_gss is true without gctx, pg_GSS_have_cred_cache must succeed or gssencmode must not be 'r'.
If SSL is enabled and allow_ssl_try is true, wait_ssl_try is false, and ssl_in_use is false, pqPacketSend of the SSL request must succeed.

L690: !conn->ssl_in_use
L706: if (pqPacketSend(conn, 0, &pv, sizeof(pv)) != STATUS_OK)
L711: goto error_return;

executions.claim: pqBuildStartupPacket3 must return non-NULL and pqPacketSend of the startup packet must succeed.
In CONNECTION_SSL_STARTUP, if ssl_in_use is false, pqReadData must return >0 and pqGetc must succeed.
After successful SSL negotiation, conn->inCursor must equal conn->inEnd.
executions.evidence:
L861: if (conn->inCursor != conn->inEnd)
L865: goto error_return;

executions.claim: In CONNECTION_GSS_STARTUP, if try_gss is true and gctx is false, pqReadData must return >0 and pqGetc must succeed.
If server responds 'N' to GSSAPI negotiation and gssencmode is 'r', execution goes to error_return.
After successful GSSAPI negotiation, conn->inCursor must equal conn->inEnd.
executions.evidence:
L973: if (conn->inCursor != conn->inEnd)
L977: goto error_return;

executions.claim: If GSSAPI negotiation fails and gssencmode is 'p', retry once; otherwise return pollres.
In CONNECTION_AWAITING_RESPONSE, beresp must be 'R' or 'E'.
executions.evidence:
L1033: if (!(beresp == 'R' || beresp == 'E'))
L1038: goto error_return;

executions.claim: If beresp is 'R', msgLength must be between 8 and 2000 inclusive.
executions.evidence:
L1058: if (beresp == 'R' && (msgLength < 8 || msgLength > 2000))
L1063: goto error_return;

executions.claim: If beresp is 'E' and msgLength is outside [8,30000], the pre-3.0 error path is taken.
executions.evidence: L1066: if (beresp == 'E' && (msgLength < 8 || msgLength > 30000))

executions.claim: After subtracting 4, msgLength must be <= conn->inEnd - conn->inCursor to process the message body.
If error SQLSTATE is ERRCODE_CANNOT_CONNECT_NOW, try_next_host is set and execution continues.
If gssenc is true and gssencmode is 'p', retry once without GSS.
If areq is AUTH_REQ_OK, status becomes CONNECTION_AUTH_OK and asyncStatus becomes PGASYNC_BUSY.
In CONNECTION_AUTH_OK, if PQgetResult returns non-NULL, either the result is a fatal error with appname unknown (retry) or execution goes to error_return.
In CONNECTION_CHECK_TARGET, for read-write/read-only targets, if either read-only flag is unknown, a query is sent and status becomes CONNECTION_CHECK_WRITABLE.
executions.evidence:
L1319: if (conn->target_server_type == SERVER_TYPE_READ_WRITE ||
L1320: conn->target_server_type == SERVER_TYPE_READ_ONLY)
L1331: if (conn->default_transaction_read_only == PG_BOOL_UNKNOWN ||
L1332: conn->in_hot_standby == PG_BOOL_UNKNOWN)
L1341: if (!PQsendQueryContinue(conn,
L1342: "SHOW transaction_read_only"))
L1343: goto error_return;
L1345: conn->status = CONNECTION_CHECK_WRITABLE;

executions.claim: In CONNECTION_CHECK_TARGET, for primary/standby/prefer-standby targets, if in_hot_standby is unknown, a query is sent and status becomes CONNECTION_CHECK_STANDBY.
executions.evidence:
L1377: else if (conn->target_server_type == SERVER_TYPE_PRIMARY ||
L1378: conn->target_server_type == SERVER_TYPE_STANDBY ||
L1379: conn->target_server_type == SERVER_TYPE_PREFER_STANDBY)
L1392: if (conn->in_hot_standby == PG_BOOL_UNKNOWN)

L1402: "SELECT pg_catalog.pg_is_in_recovery()"))
L1403: goto error_return;
L1405: conn->status = CONNECTION_CHECK_STANDBY;

executions.claim: In CONNECTION_CHECK_WRITABLE, if PQgetResult returns a result with PGRES_TUPLES_OK and one tuple, the value is used to set read-only flags; otherwise error handling and try_next_host.
In CONNECTION_CHECK_STANDBY, if PQgetResult returns a result with PGRES_TUPLES_OK and one tuple, the value is used to set in_hot_standby; otherwise error handling and try_next_host.
